LONDON BOROUGH OF THRAPSTON — PLANNING COMMITTEE
Officer report (extract), application 26/AP/0812
Site: land at 30-38 Pentworth Row, London X12 8QR
Proposal: demolition of the existing two storey warehouse and erection of a part 9, part 14
storey building comprising 118 residential units, flexible commercial floorspace at ground
floor, landscaping, cycle parking and associated works.
Recommendation: GRANT subject to conditions and a section 106 agreement.
This is an invented extract written for testing a document finder.

1. SITE AND SURROUNDINGS
1.1 The application site measures 0.34 hectares and is bounded by Pentworth Row to the south
and the disused railway cutting to the north.
1.2 The nearest residential building is Xander House, 22 Pentworth Row, whose south east
elevation lies approximately 32 metres from the nearest point of the proposed 14 storey
element and approximately 18 metres from the proposed 9 storey element.
1.3 Harrowden Street Conservation Area lies 240 metres to the west. The site is not within
the conservation area and contains no listed building.
1.4 The site is in Flood Zone 1 and is not at risk of tidal or fluvial flooding.

2. DAYLIGHT AND SUNLIGHT
2.1 The submitted daylight and sunlight assessment tests 214 windows in surrounding
residential buildings against the BRE guidance.
2.2 Of the 96 windows tested at Xander House, 71 meet the vertical sky component target of
27 per cent. A further 18 windows retain between 20 and 27 per cent.
2.3 Seven windows on the lower three floors of the south east elevation of Xander House
would fall to between 12 and 18 per cent vertical sky component, a reduction of more than 20
per cent against the existing value. The officer considers this a moderate adverse effect on
a small number of habitable rooms.
2.4 No window at Xander House above the sixth floor experiences a material reduction.

3. NOISE AND CONSTRUCTION IMPACT
3.1 The environmental health officer raises no objection subject to conditions.
3.2 The construction programme is estimated at 31 months from commencement.
3.3 A construction logistics plan and a demolition method statement are required before any
work begins on site.
3.4 Piling is expected to run for approximately 14 weeks and is the noisiest phase.

4. TRANSPORT
4.1 The site has a public transport accessibility level of 5.
4.2 Thrapston Green underground station is 480 metres walking distance from the site
entrance, and the nearest bus stop is 90 metres away on Pentworth Row.
4.3 The scheme is car free with the exception of 4 blue badge bays.
4.4 236 long stay and 12 short stay cycle parking spaces are proposed.

5. CONSULTATION
5.1 172 neighbour letters were sent. 41 responses were received, of which 33 objected.
5.2 The grounds of objection were loss of daylight, construction noise, overlooking from the
9 storey element, and pressure on local health services.
5.3 The residents association of Xander House objected on the grounds of the 18 metre
separation distance to the 9 storey element.

6. CONDITIONS
Condition 4 — Hours of working
No demolition or construction work, and no delivery to or removal from the site, shall take
place outside the hours of 08:00 to 18:00 Monday to Friday and 08:00 to 13:00 on Saturday,
and at no time on Sunday or a public holiday.
Reason: to protect the amenity of neighbouring residential occupiers.

Condition 5 — Construction environmental management plan
No development shall commence until a construction environmental management plan, including
dust suppression, wheel washing, vibration monitoring and a named site liaison officer, has
been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
Reason: to protect the amenity of neighbouring residential occupiers.

Condition 9 — Piling method statement
No piling shall take place until a piling method statement has been submitted to and
approved in writing by the local planning authority. The statement shall demonstrate that
ground borne vibration at the facade of Xander House does not exceed the limits in the
approved assessment.
Reason: to protect the amenity of neighbouring residential occupiers.

Condition 14 — Scaffolding and hoarding
Details of any scaffold, hoarding or gantry over the public highway on Pentworth Row shall
be submitted to and approved in writing before it is erected, and it shall be removed within
14 days of the completion of the works to which it relates.
Reason: in the interests of highway safety and visual amenity.

Condition 21 — Obscure glazing
The windows in the north east elevation of block B at second, third and fourth floor level
shall be fitted with obscure glazing to level 4 or above and shall be non opening below 1.7
metres from finished floor level, and shall be retained as such.
Reason: to prevent overlooking of Xander House at a separation distance of 18 metres.

7. CONCLUSION
7.1 The scheme delivers 118 homes of which 41 are affordable by habitable room.
7.2 The harm to daylight at seven windows of Xander House, and the temporary harm from a 31
month construction programme, are outweighed by the public benefits of the scheme.
7.3 Approval is recommended subject to the conditions above and the completion of a section
106 agreement within six months of the committee resolution.
